scenarioName: Difficult IV Access — Septic Dehydrated Geriatric Patient

scenarioStory.history: Daughter called 911 after finding her mother more confused than usual, weak, and reporting she has barely eaten or had anything to drink for the past 3 days due to nausea. Patient has felt feverish on and off. Skin is dry with poor turgor. No vomiting or diarrhea reported, but patient does report burning with urination for the past two days.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find a 78-year-old female with altered mental status, dry mucous membranes, poor skin turgor, and tachycardia. She is oriented to person only and slow to answer questions. → Vascular access attempted: Crew attempts peripheral IV access on fragile, dehydrated veins. Two attempts fail due to poor vein quality and hypovolemia; over 90 seconds elapses without successful access. → IO placed, fluid bolus started: IO access is obtained and a pressure-infused isotonic fluid bolus is administered toward a MAP goal of 65 mmHg. Vital signs begin to trend toward improved perfusion. → MAP improves toward goal: Perfusion improves following IO fluid resuscitation. Mental status clears further and vital signs trend toward normal as the patient is transported with advance hospital notification.

patientInformation.patientCondition: Weakness and confusion, poor oral intake for several days

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew arrives to find a 78-year-old female with altered mental status, dry mucous membranes, poor skin turgor, and tachycardia. She is oriented to person only and slow to answer questions.

scenarioEvents.name: Vascular access attempted
scenarioEvents.description: Crew attempts peripheral IV access on fragile, dehydrated veins. Two attempts fail due to poor vein quality and hypovolemia; over 90 seconds elapses without successful access.
relatedChecklist: Recognize signs of distributive (septic) shock: AMS, tachycardia, hypotension for age
Place IO needle after 2 failed peripheral IV attempts / over 90 seconds
Check blood glucose; correct if less than 60 mg/dL

scenarioEvents.name: IO placed, fluid bolus started
scenarioEvents.description: IO access is obtained and a pressure-infused isotonic fluid bolus is administered toward a MAP goal of 65 mmHg. Vital signs begin to trend toward improved perfusion.
relatedChecklist: Isotonic fluid bolus 500 mL pressure-infused via IO over <15 min toward MAP goal 65 mmHg
Provide advance notification to receiving hospital for suspected sepsis

scenarioEvents.name: MAP improves toward goal
scenarioEvents.description: Perfusion improves following IO fluid resuscitation. Mental status clears further and vital signs trend toward normal as the patient is transported with advance hospital notification.
relatedChecklist: Reassess vital signs and mental status serially en route

scenarioEvents.name: Peripheral attempts continue past threshold
scenarioEvents.description: Crew continues attempting peripheral IV access well beyond the 90-second/two-attempt threshold. Fluid resuscitation is delayed, and the patient's perfusion continues to worsen.
relatedChecklist: Abandon further peripheral attempts; place IO needle immediately and start fluid bolus
